scenes.name: Cantautores de los setenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: James Taylor se convierte, misteriosamente, en el prototipo del cantautor de los setenta; Carole King, Carly Simon y Don McLean, sobrevalorados. Las innovaciones llegan del oeste: Randy Newman y sus viñetas urbanas con fusión de estilos populares, Shawn Phillips, J.J. Cale y su estilo «laid-back», Gram Parsons, Emmylou Harris, Roger McGuinn, Jackson Browne (Late For The Sky) y, sobre todo, Tom Waits, discípulo de Beefheart y cronista de marginados (Swordfishtrombones, Rain Dogs). Excéntricos como Todd Rundgren y Annette Peacock; en Gran Bretaña, Peter Hammill, Anthony Moore, Richard Thompson, Robert Calvert, John Cale, Kevin Coyne, Elton John y los ex Beatles. El realismo de Bruce Springsteen, verdadero heredero de Woody Guthrie y del blues, y la escuela italiana de cantautores (De André, Guccini, Battisti, Sorrenti).

podcast.title: Pilot and Plane Owner in Jamaican Shooting (1996)
podcast.body: On January 16, 1996, Jimmy Buffett was at the controls of his Grumman HU-16C plane, "Hemisphere Dancer," while taxing at Negril airport in Jamaica, with Bono and his family onboard. The plane was mistakenly fired upon by Jamaican police who believed it was involved in drug running. Following the incident, Buffett penned the song "Jamaica Mistaica" about the event. "He's talking about his family. It was very scary. Let me tell you."

podcast.title: "Parrothead" Alcohol Sales Influence
podcast.body: Jimmy Buffett is an artist known for his dedicated fanbase, often referred to as "Parrotheads," who reliably consume significant amounts of alcohol at his concerts. This strong fan reputation allows Buffett to demand and receive a share of alcohol sales, sometimes leading to him earning 105% or more of ticket sales. "Jimmy Buffett is one of those acts because his fans, the parrots, will reliably drink a lot at every show. And Jimmy will get 105% of ticket sales."

podcast.title: Billionaire Status
podcast.body: Jimmy Buffett achieved billionaire status, confirmed by Forbes, largely through the strength of his songs about the tropical lifestyle, but also significantly through his ventures into best-selling novels, restaurants, hotels, resorts, and cruise ships. He once stated, "If you're an artist, if you want to have control of your life Then you got to be a businessman like it or not," a philosophy he embodied, even owning stock in Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway. "Forbes confirms that Jimmy Buffett is a billionaire and they have this quote If you're an artist, if you want to have control of your life Then you got to be a businessman like it or not Jimmy Buffett said that and he is that he is a businessman."

podcast.title: Career Background
podcast.body: Prior to achieving musical fame, Jimmy Buffett had a diverse career path, including studying journalism in college, experiencing a period as a failed Nashville songwriter, and working as a reporter for Billboard magazine. "A journalism major in college, a failed Nashville songwriter A former reporter for Billboard who writes witty and unconventional songs."

podcast.title: Critical Reception & Personal Philosophy
podcast.body: Critics frequently dismissed Buffett's music as "lightweight" or "novelty." In a 1996 interview with music journalist Mark Kemp, Buffett shared that such reviews initially hurt his feelings, particularly comments that praised the crowd but disparaged the music. He eventually stopped reading reviews, asserting that critics lacked understanding of the challenge involved in commanding the attention of 25,000 people and concluded that it was acceptable if some didn't "get" his music, as enough people did. "He said, it used to hurt my feelings because people would review me and say the crowd was amazing to watch but the music sucked And I'd go, how can you say that? Unless you walk on a stage and test your own ability to command the attention of 25,000 people You don't have any clue as to what it feels like So I quit reading everything, if they don't get it, it's fine Because enough people do."

podcast.title: Pilot and Songwriter
podcast.body: Jimmy Buffett is an accomplished pilot who owned the Grumman HU-16 C plane, "Hemisphere Dancer." He was at the controls when the plane, carrying Bono and his family, was mistakenly fired upon by Jamaican police at Negril airport in 1996. Following this incident, Buffett wrote a song about the experience, "Jamaica Mistaica." "Buffett was at the controls. He's also a pilot."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tropical Lifestyle Authenticity
podcast.body: Buffett genuinely lived the tropical sun-and-booze lifestyle that formed the core subject matter of his songs. This authenticity meant that when he sang about laid-back living and drinking, he truly meant it, rather than simply adopting a persona for commercial purposes. "It doesn't seem that Buffett was playing up the idea of drinking and living the laid-back lifestyle Just to sell his records, he was living that lifestyle as much as he could anyway So, when he sang songs like this, I think he really meant it."
